observationsNotFindings: This entry is short because it has no operands, and that is the right shape for what it does. D-169 had to specify a unique before-string, an after-string and an insertion point because it edited the register; D-170 edits nothing, so the whole surface a reviewer must check is its factual claims. Every one of those resolved against live bytes, and the masthead's own class assignment — no-cell-edit branch, not a three-limb act, not a required-now successor — is corroborated by the two precedents it names.

The one claim I nearly passed over was that class assignment, which is exactly the kind of masthead provenance sentence I have twice this session failed to test. I resolved it: D-164 and D-168 both open 'RULE-GOVERNED. Records independent dual …' and both say 'Does not edit file 08', while D-169 opens 'RULE-GOVERNED three-limb act. D-001 MF-6 file-08 write'. The branches are real and D-170 is in the one it claims.

Item 2 is careful in the place this entry could most easily overreach. Recording that the unnamed-remainder half of OBL-JOIN-FX-EXECUTION is closed sits one sentence away from implying the obligation is discharged; the draft instead names the surviving remainder as G32 execution, keeps the four authoring and BLK obligations in leftover-design, and adds 'Naming is not execution. Not QUALIFIED.' The entry that records a closure is the one most tempted to overstate it.

The Stage A pin for my own verdict resolves to bytes I amended twice after first publishing — once for a miscounted attack tally and once to record the Codex counterpart's mid-review appearance. Neither earlier digest would have resolved. That the chain carries the corrected version is the digest discipline working across a reviewer's own self-corrections, which is worth noting given how many of those this chain has now accumulated.
